# Disconnect-ZbxServer

## SYNOPSIS

Closes a connection and removes it from the session.

## SYNTAX

```
Disconnect-ZbxServer [[-Name] <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Disconnect-ZbxServer cmdlet closes the connection named in -Name, or the current one, and removes it from the session's context; a call still in flight on it finishes first. When it closes the current connection, no connection is current until Connect-ZbxServer makes one. It sends no logout, so an API token stays valid. It writes nothing.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Close a named connection

```powershell
Disconnect-ZbxServer -Name 'staging'
(Get-ZbxContext).Servers.Keys
```

-Name is the name the connection was given by Connect-ZbxServer -Name (or its endpoint's host:port). A call still in flight on it finishes first. Without -Name, the current server is closed.

### Example 2: Close a connection a script opened, even when the script fails

```powershell
$staging = Connect-ZbxServer -Uri 'https://zabbix.example/api_jsonrpc.php' -ApiToken $token -Name 'staging' -NoDefault -PassThru
try {
    Get-ZbxHost -Group 'Linux servers' -Connection $staging -CountOutput
}
finally {
    $staging | Disconnect-ZbxServer
}
```

-Name binds from the Name property of a piped connection object, so the object -PassThru wrote can be piped straight back in a finally block.

## PARAMETERS

### -Name

The connection's name; the current server when omitted.
